chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from al-Muthanna, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: 'One is only argued with (or quarrels) if he is one who has doubts, or one who has no piety (war').'

key_terms.شَاكٌّ: one who has doubts / a doubter
key_terms.يُخَاصَمُ: is argued with / is quarrelled with

ai.seo_question: Who are the only people that argue or debate according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Tawhid*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to establish a psychological and spiritual diagnostic for theological disputes, linking the act of 'khasama' (contentious argument) directly to internal states of doubt (*shakk*) or moral deficiency (*lack of war'*). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis that true certainty (*yaqin*) is characterized by humility and peace, whereas persistent debate often signals a lack of deep conviction or piety. The narration serves as a practical guideline for distinguishing between sincere inquiry and ego-driven contention in matters of creed.
